title: I Let the Mosaic-Table Booking Catch the Resident Who Hoarded the Tesserae

parts.text: I sat at table four at 1:08 p.m. and resident Lumen was already sorting my numbered tesserae. The slate said: ONE TABLE. TWO HOURS. TILE STAYS WITH THE BOOKING. I was forty-one, studio member, holding a color card that listed our palette. Lumen shrugged. "Residents are the table." I photographed the slate, the booking, and her bins on my nippers. Then I asked for the table log. At 1:16 the studio pinged why Lumen's name was on my tile. I kept my voice studio-soft and let the timestamp talk. A slate is only a slate until someone treats it like a clock.
parts.cliffhanger_hint: The studio can see Lumen's bins on my nippers during our booking.

social.video_title: She sorted my numbered tesserae into her bins — Part 1/2
social.description: Mosaic table, a resident on my nippers, a two-hour slate she posted. I logged the bins. Would you have asked for the table log?

parts.text: Lumen called it a sort until the studio asked for the photo. I printed the ticket, the slate, and the bins still. The tesserae went back to my tray. Lumen ran her own two hours and told the next resident atmosphere was always about grout. Grout is a word residents use when a booking exists. Table policy now has a second line: RESIDENTS ARE NOT THE TABLE. I keep our tile on a labeled bin. Lumen brown-bags her jokes. The studio finally looks like a booking, not a loan. The rule looks ordinary now, which is the whole point.

social.video_title: Residents are not the table — Part 2/2
social.description: Table log, numbered tesserae, and a second line on the slate. Was a sort ever my nippers?
